chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Idris narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Yahya b. 'Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Nahawandi from Muhammad b. Sulayman al-Daylami from his father. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say:
Winter is the springtime of the believer - its night is prolonged, which helps him stand in prayer; and its day is shortened, which helps him fast.

key_terms.الشِّتَاءُ رَبِيعُ الْمُؤْمِنِ: Winter is the springtime of the believer - a well-known saying encouraging worship
key_terms.صِيَامِهِ: His fasting - voluntary fasting easier with short days
key_terms.قِيَامِهِ: His standing in prayer - night prayer (tahajjud)

ai.seo_question: Why is winter called the spring of the believer in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) beautifully describes winter as the believer's spring season, because the long nights facilitate night prayer (tahajjud) and the short days make fasting easier. This metaphor reframes a season often associated with hardship as a time of spiritual opportunity.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Idris narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. yahya b. `Imran al-Ash`ari narrated to us from Ibrahim b. Ishaq al-Nahawandi from Muhammad b. Sulayman al-Daylami from his father.  He said: I heard Aba `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) say:
Winter is the springtime of the believer – night is prolonged in it, which helps him stand up in prayer in it; and its day is shortened, which helps him fast in it.
